author: Ford Lascari
content:
Hello sunshine team!

I was heavily involved in the melee decomp and built the harness that led to mass sweeping improvements.

I was planning on running a round on Sunshine to see how it performs on a new game that is also not as complete as melee was when I joined in.

With this in mind, are there any documented code standards that would differ significantly than melee before doing a first run?

author: Mrkol
content: do you want to do a sweep of fixing existing stuff or decompiling new stuff?

author: Mrkol
content: cuz I don't have the capacity to check & clean up clanker decompiled TUs rn, there are already a few PRs pending

author: Mrkol
content:
No written docs, but off the top of my head:
- extract maximum info from the symbol map(s) of sms and other games and use it
- reconstruct UNUSED dead-stripped functions where possible from inlining & validate with the map size (we have a validate symbol order script)
- don't use tricks like `char trash[4]` for (fake)matching stack frame sizes, better to leave it non-matching

author: Mrkol
content: oh, and I don't trust clankers with naming things, I manually check every name they propose

author: Ford Lascari
content:
TLDR I can do both, I had worked with the melee team over the months by taking all their PR review comments and turning them into lint rules that fail before any change is allowed to be added to the PR.

I believe those rules you mentioned are covered in that, but I will confirm.
- I dealt with a lot of the fake match slop, and by the end there were nearly no slop issues, but this may have been due to code largely being complete so it had clear code quality to pull from.
- Naming is specifically linted for (ie, no renaming of anything, doing so causes a failure)

---

The general process I had done in the pass is it opens up one large PR as a draft and it can either be merged in directly, broken down, or the most common thing was as the system ran, others would pull from it to complete matches from the improvements listed in the CI.

I'd be running it as an experiment either way to see how it can perform with less context and on a new game
- I would not be surprised in like a 10%+ jump given the amount of open files and such, but I need to actually run it to see what happens

Its obv up to yourself and other maintainers with what you do with the branch, just wanted to make sure I try to respect the standards y'all have put in place as much as possible.

author: Mrkol
content: the how of it is: you filter out all lines from the MAP by `.*FileName.cpp` and then paste the mangled names into `./bulk_demangle.sh` -- and there you have it, full list of symbols (functions & global variables) that you should define in this TU

author: Mrkol
content: oh, and you have to reverse the order

author: Mrkol
content: because all game TUs are compiled with the `-inline deferred` flag, the map contains the symbols in reverse order

author: Mrkol
content: declaring & defining all of them

author: Mrkol
content: the reason for this is that having the names/apis helps you understand the class better AND sometimes you must use the unused functions to properly match the used ones -- because UNUSED stuff got inlined and you cannot get the correct codegen without using inlining yourself

author: Mrkol
content: this is extremely common in enemy files -- UNUSED stuff is not actually unused, it was just inlined

author: Mrkol
content: We have a mystery on our hands. In TMarNameRefGen::getNameRef, TSunGlass's ctor gets inlined for us but is not in the target. How do we make it not inline? One way would be to make TColor non-trivial (add a destructor), but that breaks matches in a whole bunch of other places where it is clearly compiled as a trivial type. Also no such dtor in the TWW debug maps. Statement count doesn't work here -- turns out methods whose bodies are defined inside of the class body don't have the statement heuristic and always get inlined. The last thing that could help is call stack depth -- but why would this constructor be nested within other inlines? Makes no sense to me... hence, the mystery
